title: Elastic Quota Manager and Graceful Degradation — PRD (sketch)
body:
Overview:

This doc proposes the Elastic Quota Manager (EQM) — a control plane + runtime component for Dedicated capacity that enforces tenant quotas while allowing controlled, observable bursts and graceful degradation under contention. The goal is to give teams predictable reserved throughput while enabling safe elasticity to absorb real-world traffic spikes with clear operator semantics.

Problem statement:
- Customers buy reserved capacity but real workloads have spiky behaviors (sync calls, batch jobs, traffic surges) that are hard to dimension.
- Current options are: rigid reservation (wastes capacity) or permissive burst pools (uncontrolled interference and SLA violations).
- Platform operators lack a single primitive that: enforces isolation, enables bounded burst, supports preemption and graceful user-level fallback, and exposes clear accounting.

High-level objectives (measurable):
1) Preserve per-tenant 99th percentile latency SLOs for reserved capacity workloads during normal operation (target: <= configured SLO + 10ms).
2) Allow bounded bursts up to X× baseline for short windows while keeping cross-tenant tail latency impact < 5% regression compared to baseline.
3) Provide deterministic billing/chargeback semantics for burst usage (metered and visible within console) with accuracy within 2%.
4) Offer operators clear signals and controls for emergency throttles, preemptions, and recovery.

Non-goals:
- Replacing Dedicated autoscaler entirely: EQM augments autoscaling with per-tenant policy enforcement and burst accounting.
- Solving model-level quality regressions caused by quantization/variants.

Key concepts and terminology:
- Baseline capacity: the tenant's committed GPUs/throughput guaranteed under reservation.
- Elastic burst allowance: temporary capacity above baseline available from a shared burst pool or from unused reserved headroom of other tenants (configurable per deployment).
- Soft limit: a per-tenant throughput cap that can be exceeded temporarily (consumes burst tokens); triggers warnings and optional client-level hints.
- Hard limit: absolute cap that immediately rejects/queues requests when exceeded.
- Burst tokens / credits: accounting units consumed when tenant uses elastic capacity; tokens decay or are billed.
- Grace window: short time window where the system transitions from permissive burst to enforced throttling to avoid abrupt failures for client apps.

User scenarios / user stories:
- As a product engineer, I want short spikes up to 3× baseline for 30s to succeed without my team having to buy more capacity.
- As an SRE, I want a predictable way to preempt burst consumption from low-priority tenants during region-level pressure.
- As a finance owner, I want detailed burst usage invoices and per-route chargebacks for credit consumption.

Configuration primitives (surface in Console/API):
- min_capacity (int): lower bound reserved capacity units that cannot be scaled below.
- baseline_capacity (int): committed units (e.g., GPU slices or tokens/sec) for billing and isolation.
- soft_limit_rate (float): TPS or token/sec beyond baseline that will consume burst credits.
- hard_limit_rate (float): absolute reject threshold.
- burst_allowance_window (duration): maximum contiguous time a tenant may consume elastic capacity at > baseline (default 30s).
- burst_bucket_size (int): number of burst tokens pre-funded for a tenant (optional prepaid credits).
- preempt_policy (enum): [none, best-effort, strict] — behavior for reclaiming capacity under pressure.

Runtime model (sketch):
1) Admission point tracks per-tenant current_rate and baseline_capacity.
2) For requests exceeding baseline but below soft_limit_rate, EQM consumes burst tokens and admits request.
3) If burst tokens exhausted and within burst_allowance_window, EQM can fall back to best-effort borrowing from global burst pool (if enabled) subject to global headroom and tenant priority.
4) If above hard_limit_rate, EQM either queues (short queue with timeout) or rejects based on client preference.
5) When preempt_policy triggers, low-priority tenants get soft-capped preferentially; strict preemptions enforce immediate reclaim.

APIs and Console UX (example):
- PATCH /v1/dedicated/{tenant_id}/quota {"baseline_capacity": 8, "soft_limit_rate": 80.0, "hard_limit_rate": 120.0, "burst_bucket_size": 100000}
- Console toggles: enable_global_burst_pool (boolean), tenant_priority (P0..P4), invoice_burst_monthly (boolean).
- Console view: timeseries of baseline vs actual, burst token balance, per-route breakdown, projected cost if current burn rate continues.

Billing and accounting model:
- Two streams: 1) committed usage charged at reserved rates; 2) burst usage charged at on-demand premium or consumed from prepaid bucket.
- Burst meters: tokens consumed by token-per-inference or token-per-second depending on configuration.
- Billing granularity: 1-minute windows with rollup in UI; invoicing exported to billing pipeline daily.

Operator controls and runbook (initial runbook steps):
- Signals to watch: global_burst_pool_utilization > 70%, region_tail_latency_increase > 15%, burst_token_balance_negative_count > 0.
- Emergency actions: toggle enable_global_burst_pool=false, escalate strict preempt_policy, move critical tenants to isolation lane.
- Recovery: perform soft throttles, backfill tenant burst buckets from unallocated reserved capacity, run sanity checks on routing fallbacks.

Telemetry and metrics (names and descriptions):
- eqm.tenant.{tenant_id}.baseline_usage_pct (gauge)
- eqm.tenant.{tenant_id}.burst_tokens_balance (gauge)
- eqm.tenant.{tenant_id}.burst_burn_rate_per_min (counter)
- eqm.global.burst_pool_utilization (gauge)
- eqm.region.preemptions.count (counter)
- eqm.latency.p99.by_tenant (histogram)
- eqm.rejections.by_reason (counter with tags: hard_limit, queued_timeout, preempted)
- alerts: eqm.global.burst_pool_utilization > 85% for 5m, eqm.region.preemptions.count spikes > 10/min

Failure modes and mitigations:
- Unbounded burst burn: detect and auto-block tenants exceeding configured burst_bucket_size; send a billing alert and throttle.
- Starvation of low-priority tenants: preempt_policy default should be best-effort; strict preemptions only after operator confirmation or automated escalation path.
- Observability blind spots: ensure per-tenant metrics are emitted even when tenant is idle (0-values) and add debug traces for admission decisions.

Compatibility with Dedicated autoscaler and placement:
- EQM will surface realtime utilization signals to autoscaler: baseline headroom, burst_pool pressure, and per-tenant trends so autoscaler can make placement decisions.
- For burst usage served by spare reserved capacity (other tenants’ unused headroom), EQM must coordinate with placement to ensure cross-tenant isolation constraints (affinity, tenancy) are honored.

Rollout plan (phased):
- Phase 0 (internal alpha, 4 weeks): implement basic token bucket admission + per-tenant tokens, telemetry, and local operator toggles; test on internal tenants.
- Phase 1 (canary with partner customers, 6–8 weeks): enable global burst pool optional; collect billing signals and tail latency metrics; iterate on preempt_policy.
- Phase 2 (wider release, 8–12 weeks): console controls, billing integration, rollout to Dedicated customers as opt-in.
- Phase 3 (GA): default enablement for new tenants, docs and runbooks, SRE playbook.

Experiment ideas / open questions:
- Can we safely allow cross-tenant borrowing from other tenants' unused reservation with consent/markets? (pricing + compliance concerns)
- Explore machine-learned burst forecasts to pre-warm capacity or pre-issue temporary credits.
- How to represent burst allowances in SLA language? Should we surface probabilistic guarantees?

Security and compliance notes:
- Any cross-tenant borrowing must obey data isolation constraints; ensure no KV cache or model state is shared across reclaimed capacity.
- Audit logs: all preemptions and burst assignments must have immutable audit trail (who/why/when).

Dependencies and assumptions:
- Requires admission control hook in serving runtime with low overhead (<1–2ms median).
- Billing pipeline must accept minute-level metering input for burst tokens.
- Console must support new tenant-level widgets.

Next steps / immediate action items:
- Align on burst_token accounting unit with finance (action: Jorge, due 2025-11-21).
- Spike: implement light-weight token bucket admission prototype in serving runtime (owner: Ethan, 2 weeks).
- Draft UI mockups for console (owner: Maya, 1 week).

Appendix: Example admission traces (human-readable):
- At t=00:00 tenant A baseline=100rps, soft_limit_rate=150rps, burst_bucket=500tokens.
- At t=00:05 CPU spike - request rate jumps to 260rps. EQM consumes 110 tokens over 10s, then dips into global pool for next 20s. At t=00:40 global pool hits 90% util -> SRE trigger -> global_burst_pool disabled -> EQM enforces tenant hard_limit and begins reject/queue path. Billing records consumed tokens for tenant A.

Notes on uniqueness vs existing drafts:
- This doc emphasizes a combined accounting + graceful-degradation primitive (tokens + grace window) instead of only autoscaling or eviction plays. It surfaces operator runbook and billing integration early to avoid the common platform/finance misalignment.

End of sketch.
